paper_title: Towards Predicting Any Human Trajectory In Context
caption: Performance of random example selection and the proposed STES at varying numbers of in-context examples with a larger number of examples
model_annotation: The plot illustrates minADE\(_{20}\) (with a downward arrow indicating lower values are preferable) as a function of the number of in-context examples, showing two methods labeled “ST-ES” and “Random.” The x-axis is labeled “Number of Examples,” uses a linear scale, and spans from 0 to 15 with labeled ticks at 0, 5, 10, and 15. The y-axis is labeled “minADE\(_{20}\) (↓),” uses a linear scale, and displays labeled ticks at 15.0, 15.5, 16.0, 16.5, and 17.0 (with the plotted values extending slightly above 17.0 and slightly below 15.0). The ST-ES series is drawn as a solid blue line with circular markers; it starts near 17.1 at 0 examples, drops sharply to about 15.2 at 1 example, then continues downward more gradually into the mid–14.7 range by around 5 examples, remains near 14.7 across most of the remaining x-values, and ends around 14.7–14.8 at 15 examples. The Random series is drawn as a solid orange line with circular markers; it begins near 16.8 at 0 examples, decreases to about 16.5 at 1 example, and then stays nearly flat around 16.45–16.50 through 15 examples with only small point-to-point fluctuations.
